CL-0003.opening_line: Mrs Voss-Brenner, when we last spoke in May you said you would prefer something safe and boring, and I would like to start today by showing you plainly what your husband's portfolio actually holds and how it lines up with the tax instalment due before the end of the year.
paragraphs: Margarethe Voss-Brenner comes in as a recent widow, not as an investor. At the first meeting after the transfer in on 2026-02-16 she said several times that she does not understand what is in the portfolio, that her husband handled all of it, and that she has never taken a risk with money. She asked that nothing be changed for now. Her risk profiling came back Conservative, and her stated objectives are to understand and de-risk what she inherited, secure a stable income, and address German inheritance tax. The portfolio she holds points the other way.

PF-0005 holds 71.46% in Equity against a Conservative band of 10-30%, and 9.15% in Fixed Income against a band of 45-75%. Both breaches are classified as inherited: the portfolio came across as it stood and there is no client-initiated trade into either class. Nobody chose this allocation, neither the bank nor Mrs Voss-Brenner, which makes it a different conversation from a drift she sat through. Her message of 2026-05-29, asking whether the news from the Middle East would affect her portfolio and saying she would prefer 'something safe and boring', is the same concern in her own words. One caveat before any sale is discussed: SYN-ST-0107 carries no cost basis in our data, so the tax consequence of selling it to correct the equity position cannot be stated from what we hold.

The German inheritance tax instalment of EUR 3,400,000 (USD 3,712,800) falls due by 2026-12-31 and represents 16.74% of the portfolio. Holdings sellable daily or weekly come to 88.29%, covering it 5.27 times, so the money can be raised. But cash and fixed income together are only 16.83%, or 1.01 times the bill, which means meeting it involves selling into the rest of the portfolio rather than drawing on near-cash. Note that 5.39% is illiquid and 6.32% monthly-dealing is excluded from available funds, and private-market valuations in that group lag by a quarter as a matter of industry practice, so that excluded value is indicative rather than current.

The tax deadline and the de-risking she has asked for may be one exercise rather than two, since both require reducing the equity weight. Given that the megacap technology complex briefly shed around USD 2 trillion in market value on 2026-06-05 on AI capital expenditure concerns before recovering later in the month, the sequencing and timing of any sales is worth raising with her, alongside what a stable income stream would look like once Fixed Income is brought back toward its band. You may want to check how much she now understands about the underlying holdings, given what she told us in February.

CL-0014.opening_line: Mr Lau, before we turn to the Mid-Levels contribution, I would like to walk through how much of the portfolio moves on a single name — including the part that would move in your favour.
paragraphs: Lau Chi Ming, 63, built his wealth developing Hong Kong residential and commercial property, and the portfolio is essentially a second copy of that business. Looking through the structured product to the names it references, 49.03% sits in Real Estate across four positions in four asset classes, which is why it does not read as concentration on the statement. Within that, Golden Harbour Properties Ltd is held three ways — equity, fixed income and the structured product — for 29.45% of the portfolio, and each line sits under a different limit, so no single concentration check sees the whole position. The 12M accumulator references names he already owns outright as Golden Harbour Properties 5.25% Perpetual (12.87%) and Golden Harbour Properties Ltd (9.54%), so it adds to the position rather than spreading it; on the downside a worst-of basket pays on whichever underlying falls furthest. Your note of 2026-03-05 records you making this point to him, and his answer that the shared bet is precisely why he is confident.

Separately, Equity is 23.39% against the balanced mandate's 30-55% band, below the floor. No client-initiated trade explains it — the weights moved through market action, so the exposure changed without anyone deciding it should. It is classified as drift and reported as a mandate breach in its own right.

The HKD 60,000,000 equity contribution for the Mid-Levels redevelopment is due by 2027-06-30 and represents 29.00% of the portfolio, and your 2026-08-11 note records he expects to fund it partly from here and was surprised how little is sellable. On paper, daily and weekly holdings cover it 2.53 times over, but free liquid holdings are USD 0 against a need of USD 7,682,458: the portfolio is pledged under CF-0002 with HKD 58,000,000 drawn and a loan-to-value of 69.41% against a 70% margin-call threshold, leaving 0.59 percentage points of headroom. Funding the contribution from pledged collateral takes the loan-to-value to 97.76%. On these numbers that route is not available, and it is worth raising how else the obligation would be met. Note that 26.62% of the portfolio is excluded as illiquid, and those private-market valuations lag by a quarter as a matter of industry practice.

One point cuts the other way and is worth putting in front of him. Repricing the four affected holdings to 2026-02-27, when Brent crude was 72.4 USD/barrel against 101.5 today, adds about USD 3,818,077, or 14.41% of the portfolio: the Mid-Levels apartment +0.19m, Golden Harbour Properties Ltd +0.77m, the accumulator +1.28m and the perpetual +1.58m. Oil has moved a long way since then — the 2026-02-28 commencement of US and Israeli military operations against Iran, the 2026-03-04 effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the 2026-05-04 Brent peak near USD 114, and the re-widened risk premium after the 2026-08-05 reimposition of a naval blockade. This is arithmetic over stored prices at two dates, not a forecast, and it carries no probability. What makes it worth raising is that the good news lands in exactly the same four names as the risk.

CL-0019.opening_line: Abdullah, you asked us in August what happens to this portfolio if the Strait reopens — we've now put numbers to it, and I'd like to walk you through what we found.
paragraphs: Abdullah Al-Mansoori is 49, in peak earning years, and his wealth comes from Gulf logistics, port services and marine chartering. His stated objectives are to build wealth outside the Gulf and outside the shipping sector, to fund a family office in Asia, and to grow capital long term. He made the tension explicit himself on 2026-04-15, when he subscribed the shipping and energy FCN on the view that charter rates stay elevated while the Strait situation is unresolved: he said the point of the Asia portfolio was to be uncorrelated with the Gulf business, and noted it currently is not.

Nothing in the portfolio is a breach. All five mandate bands are within range — Equity 57.97% (40-65), Fixed Income 15.67% (15-40), Structured Products 12.90% (0-15), Cash 7.45% (2-15), Alternatives 6.00% (0-25) — and the largest single line, Global Developed Equity Index Fund at 13.30%, sits under its 15% limit. What no single control sees is the aggregate: 33.20% of the portfolio names shipping directly, and once the Fixed Coupon Note ref. Basket C, 9.20% p.a., 12M is resolved to the names it references, 42.13% sits in Energy and Industrials across four positions and two asset classes. The note itself references Global Energy Majors ADR and Pacific Orient Shipping, both already held outright as Global Energy Majors Equity Fund (8.94%) and Pacific Orient Shipping Ltd (11.41%) — 33.25% of the portfolio on the same underlying, held three ways. On a worst-of basket the note pays on whichever leg falls furthest, so it adds to that position rather than spreading it. Worth raising as one conversation rather than three.

The scenario he asked about cuts against him twice. Repricing the affected holdings to 2026-02-27 levels, when Brent was 72.4 USD/barrel against 101.5 today, takes roughly USD 2,513,211 off the portfolio — 7.80%: the FCN 4.16m to 3.34m, Pacific Orient Shipping 3.68m to 2.95m, Global Energy Majors Equity Fund 2.88m to 2.34m, and Asia Pacific Shipping and Logistics Fund 2.86m to 2.43m. Since the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed on 2026-03-04 and the risk premium re-widened when the United States reimposed a naval blockade on 2026-08-05, both the operating business and the portfolio have been paid by the same conditions. A normalisation — the outcome most people would call good news — would take value from both in the same week. This is arithmetic over stored prices at two dates, not a forecast; note also that the FCN is repriced off Pacific Orient Shipping, and on a strict worst-of reading the figure would be nearer 2.65m.

Two open items. He asked on 2026-08-12 for a view on what happens to his portfolio if the Strait reopens and normalises, and the note records that we have not modelled this — it is still outstanding, and you may want to close it before he raises it again. Separately, the Singapore family office seed capital of USD 5,000,000 by 2027-12-31 is 15.52% of the portfolio; daily and weekly liquidity covers it 5.22 times, but cash and fixed income together are only 23.12%, or 1.49 times, so funding it means selling into the rest of the book rather than drawing on near-cash. That obligation is recorded as likely rather than confirmed, so it is worth checking whether the timing and amount still hold.
